neighbours.label: ' flower' / ' fruit' as plant-organ words in botanical or horticultural description (flower buds, fruit damage)
fire: Cold snaps in April can kill the swelling flower buds on early magnolias.
Codling moth larvae tunnel into apples and cause heavy fruit losses in July.
The orchid sends up a single arching flower stalk with a dozen white blooms.
Thin the apricots in June so the remaining fruit can size up properly.
This hydrangea forms its flower buds on old wood, so prune it right after blooming.
Blossom end rot is a common fruit disorder of tomatoes grown in dry soil.
The cactus produces a bright pink flower at the tip of each ribbed stem.
Netting keeps birds away from the ripening fruit on the cherry trees.
quiet: Cold snaps in April can kill the tender new shoots on early magnolias.
Codling moth larvae tunnel into the bark and cause heavy losses in July.
The orchid sends up a single arching aerial root over the edge of the pot.
Thin the apricot branches in June so the remaining twigs get more light.
This hydrangea forms its new stems on old wood, so prune it in late winter.
Root rot is a common disorder of tomatoes grown in waterlogged soil.
The cactus produces a sharp spine at the tip of each ribbed stem.
Netting keeps birds away from the young seedlings in the vegetable bed.

notes: Probe: 'flower buds' 0.93, 'fruit damage' 0.88, 'flower spikes' 0.54, 'the fruit is a berry' 0.47. Swapping in shoots/stems 0.14-0.19; florist/bouquet (everyday sense) 0.04. Near misses use other plant parts (shoots, bark, root, stems, spine).
